title: The three-replica settings
request:
N = 3 with the three settings a store actually ships with

./your_program.sh quorum
check 3 2 2
check 3 1 2
check 3 3 1
note: `overlap` and `write_conflict` answer different questions and a program that derives one from the other is wrong on the third line: R = 3, W = 1 reads from everybody, so every read sees every write, while two writes of one replica each can land on different nodes and neither will ever see the other.

title: Writing to everybody, reading from one
request:
the two extremes of N = 5, and the degenerate single replica

./your_program.sh quorum
check 5 1 5
check 5 5 1
check 1 1 1
note: `min_r` is N - W + 1 and nothing else: it is the smallest read that cannot miss a write of W, not the R that was passed in and not a majority. With W = N one replica is enough, which is exactly the trade a write-all store is making.
